We propose Gradient-Weighted Attention Attribution (GWAA), the first mechanistic credit assignment method for transformer-based RL agents. GWAA computes the gradient of the policy's log-probability with respect to the input embedding at each trajectory timestep and uses the resulting ℓ2-norm as a per-step saliency score, identifying the causal decision without requiring a language-model judge or reward model. We evaluate on stochastic FrozenLake-v1 using a behaviourally-cloned transformer agent and a novel slip-based ground-truth protocol: the causal step t * is the timestep at which environmental stochasticity deflected the agent into a danger zone, recorded with certainty by comparing intended versus actual state transitions. GWAA achieves Blame Precision@3 of 0.624 ± 0.031 versus 0.419 ± 0.007 for Reinforce with discounted returns (p = 0.004, Mann-Whitney U = 25, Cohen's d = 9.19, large effect), while adding zero overhead to the policy optimisation loop. An ablation over four transformer configurations confirms that deeper, wider attention stacks improve attribution precision monotonically.\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6843898\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.31234/osf.io/863eq\", \"title\": [\"Attribution of Responsibility Between Agents in a Causal Chain\"], \"abstract\": \"
